liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **House P.A. Music** (2 reviews): The Honky Tonk Women heard here sounds to the listener like Elton John playing it; The Honky Tonk Woman matches Elton John's 11-17-70 recording, made the next day, which the listener finds suspect [14][15]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 other source): Steve Winwood plays Pigpen's Hammond organ on this song, and on Big Railroad Blues and Not Fade Away [1]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 other source): Winwood adds backing vocals through the Not Fade Away > Goin' Down the Road > Not Fade Away sequence, including the first verse [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **House P.A. Music**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **Frozen Logger**: rare: 9 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd70-11-16.sbd.winters.17361.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 103 min; rated 3.79/5 by 28 [1]. Said about its sound: Disc 1, track 3 has analog distortion and channel dropouts, possibly from a loose plug on the master reel-to-reel; Excellent quality, with an unusual mix: Bobby far forward in the left channel, Jerry and Winwood further back, mostly right [1][7]
- **gd1970-11-16.sbd.112987.flac**: soundboard; 12 songs; 80 min; rated 0.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1970-11-16.135717.aud.petlock.flac16**: audience recording; 1 songs; 10 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Steve Winwood and Chris Wood are credited as guests; Jorma Kaukonen may appear via a Hot Tuna set with Dead members sitting in [2]
- Jorma Kaukonen appears, possibly from a Hot Tuna set in which Dead members sat in [3]
- Recalls a Fillmore East Dead show of this period simulcast on a New York radio station, lasting hours with the crowd standing throughout [11]
- The announcement came at the weekend's late Zappa show, billing the Airplane and the Dead together [13]
- Set 2 may be the tape long circulated as Andersen Theater 11/23/70, per a September 2004 deadlists.com update [2]
- Set 2 may be the tape long circulated mislabeled as Andersen Theater 11/23/70, per deadlists.com in 2004 [3]
- Set 2 is the tape long circulated, apparently mislabeled, as Anderson Theater, NYC 11/23/70 [5]
- Argues the date should be 11/23/70, since Winwood, Capaldi and Wood played these same songs then and no 11/16 show is documented [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-11-16.sbd.winters.17361.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bill Gadsden and D. Winters; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Set 2 was likely mastered by the same crew behind surreptitious soundboard masters from this venue on 5/15/70 and 9/20/70 [5]
- **gd1970-11-16.sbd.112987.flac**: source: SBD > RR > ? > ? > Cassette; Transfer Info: Nak MR2 Deck > Cassette > WAV >Soundforge > FLAC [2]
- **gd1970-11-16.135717.aud.petlock.flac16**: taped by Rich Petlock; source: Partial; [3]
